title: Secure Code Review Alert
briefing: A routine application security scan reveals potential vulnerabilities in recently deployed code. The security and development teams must determine whether the findings represent exploitable weaknesses or benign false positives.

injects.title: Additional Scan Findings
injects.message: The automated scanner reveals additional potential issues in related components, raising concern that the vulnerability may affect multiple modules.

injects.title: Developer Pushback
injects.message: Developers argue that the scanner result is likely a false positive and request that the security team validate the issue before recommending remediation.

injects.title: Compliance Review Triggered
injects.message: Internal compliance staff flag the issue as potentially affecting regulatory obligations if customer data exposure cannot be ruled out.

injects.title: Security Advisory Consideration
injects.message: Product leadership asks whether a security advisory should be prepared in case customers need to update their systems.

step_1.situation: Security scanning tools report a possible injection vulnerability in a recently deployed service endpoint. The team begins by identifying which indicators truly suggest exploitable risk.

if_correct.consequence: The team correctly identifies the most relevant security indicators and begins focused validation of the code path.

if_incorrect.consequence: Misinterpreting the scan results leads to confusion and delays targeted analysis.

step_2.situation: The team evaluates how application-layer protections and input validation mechanisms affect the likelihood of successful exploitation.

if_correct.consequence: Security engineers verify whether existing controls mitigate the vulnerability risk.

if_incorrect.consequence: Assumptions about defensive controls lead to an incomplete understanding of the vulnerability.

step_3.situation: Leadership asks whether the issue represents a confirmed vulnerability requiring urgent remediation or simply a theoretical risk.

if_correct.consequence: The team provides a clear explanation of risk and recommended remediation timelines.

if_incorrect.consequence: Unclear communication causes confusion between engineering and security teams.

step_4.situation: The team evaluates whether additional authentication or authorization controls could mitigate risk until a permanent code fix is deployed.

if_correct.consequence: Interim security controls reduce exposure while developers prepare a patch.

if_incorrect.consequence: Failure to consider mitigation controls increases potential exposure if exploitation occurs.

step_5.situation: The organization considers whether public disclosure or customer notification might eventually be required.

if_correct.consequence: Responsible communication planning preserves customer trust while remediation progresses.

if_incorrect.consequence: Poor communication planning creates risk of reputational damage if the vulnerability becomes public.
